newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PLAY RESUMES IN U.S. OPEN AFTER LIGHTNING THREAT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PLAY RESUMES IN U.S. OPEN AFTER LIGHTNING THREAT.

text.p: Play resumed in the second round of the U.S. Open on Friday afternoon after a suspension of more than two hours due to lightning in the area.
The players, who were ordered off Congressional Country Club's course at 11:52 a.m. EDT (1552 GMT) when lightning was detected nearby, were allowed back on the course at 2:10 p.m. EDT (1610 GMT).
However, the suspension meant that a number of late starters would probably not have enough time to complete their second rounds before dark.
Those players who do not finish will be required to return to the course very early on Saturday to complete their rounds before the third round begins.
Only 16 players in the 156-man field had completed play before the siren sounded to suspend play.
Colin Montgomerie of Britain, the first-round leader at five under par, was among those who had not started play when the suspension was called.
Tom Lehman, the British Open champion, was one stroke off the lead at four under after playing 16 holes of his second round. He was tied with Hal Sutton, who also had yet to begin play on Friday.
